client_alerts.headline: Meta's new Muse Wonder models ship with cross-conversation memory and no published enterprise data terms
client_alerts.body: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full (announced Oct 12) include **Active Memory**, which retains user information across conversations. Coverage so far gives no enterprise terms, retention period, or training-use statement, and Meta's detailed safety report is still pending. Advise clients to keep client data out of Muse Code and the Meta Model API until those terms are published.

client_alerts.headline: Anthropic now bills for some blocked API requests and locks earlier context on newer accounts
client_alerts.body: Anthropic's Oct 12 anti-distillation update confirms that API accounts created on or after Aug 31 cannot edit Claude's earlier context on supported models, and that since Sept 24 some requests blocked before the model responds are still charged. Anthropic acknowledges legitimate requests may occasionally be blocked. Clients running Claude integrations should review error handling and cost monitoring.

top_moves.title: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full as closed-weight agent models
top_moves.body: Meta calls them its most capable models to date, aimed at long-running tasks, computer use, and legal, finance and health work. Muse Wonder is on the Meta Model API and Muse Code; Wonder Full needs a paid Muse Code plan from **$50/month**. No open weights, benchmark claims are Meta's own, and the safety report comes later.

top_moves.title: Anthropic says anti-distillation safeguards cut reasoning extraction by 90–99%
top_moves.body: The package combines preserved thinking, a two-stage classifier across Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5/5.5 and Fable 5/5.1, and bans on thousands of accounts. The practical side effects are locked earlier context on newer API accounts, reasoning transcripts limited to the requesting organization, and **charges for some blocked requests**.

top_moves.title: OpenAI's Decisions API surfaces for fast typed yes/no and classification calls
top_moves.body: A Towards Data Science guide describes a Decisions API built on GPT-6 Luna that returns typed decisions and probabilities, which OpenAI claims run up to ten times faster than the Responses API. This rests on one secondary source and the launch date is not confirmed, so verify against OpenAI's docs before designing around it.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: A Decisions API for fast typed classification on GPT-6 Luna is being documented in secondary coverage, while GPT-6 and Intelligent UI continue rolling out.
providers.detail: A Towards Data Science guide describes the Decisions API as returning typed decisions such as yes/no probabilities, with an OpenAI claim of up to ten times the speed of the Responses API on GPT-6 Luna; the launch date is not confirmed. Release notes from Oct 6–9 remain the latest dated items: audio uploads for paid plans, faster steering in Codex, and Composer predictions in beta. A Financial Times report last week put annualized revenue roughly $20 billion below figures circulating among investors.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Anthropic says new safeguards cut reasoning-data distillation by 90–99%, with locked earlier context on newer API accounts and charges for some blocked requests.
providers.detail: The Oct 12 announcement covers preserved thinking for API accounts created on or after Aug 31, reasoning transcripts for Sonnet 5.5 limited to the requesting organization, and a two-stage classifier with a claimed false-positive rate under 0.1%. Since Sept 24 some requests blocked before the model responds are still billed. Anthropic says thousands of accounts were banned and concedes some developers must update integrations. The reported Wednesday investor day could not be re-confirmed in today's searches.
providers.alertReason: Some blocked API requests are billed and earlier context is locked on accounts created from Aug 31
